Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The England players are in a huddle and now they spread out to take their respective field positions. Dan Lawrence is in the field for the injured Ollie Robinson. Usman Khawaja and David Warner are the two openers for Australia. Stuart Broad has the new ball in hand and is raring to go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

England would have hoped for a better start as they lost both Ben Duckett and Harry Brook early on. Then Zak Crawley and Joe Root steadied things for a bit but the former got dismissed just before stumps on Day 1 and the latter along with Jonny Bairstow saw the rest of the overs.  However, the hosts once again went under pressure as the two overnight batters and local lads got out in quick succession still trailing by a good margin. Moeen Ali built up a good partnership with Ben Stokes but couldn't hang around long. As the lower order got exposed, Stokes changed his gears once again and went into overdrive scoring another fine fifty, ultimately falling on 80 runs, and Mark Wood also played a quick cameo which helped them reduce the lead massively. Join us in a bit for the second innings of Australia.

That's it for England! Yet another terrific knock from Ben Stokes! They have been bowled out for and surrendered a lead of just 26 runs to the visitors. Australia will be a bit disappointed as they would have liked to wrap up things much earlier. Pat Cummins led from the front with a brilliant six-wicket haul and looked very sharp. Mitchell Starc got two crucial wickets while Mitchell Marsh chipped in with one. Todd Murphy bowled well but got battered by Stokes before getting him out eventually. Now, their batters have a job on their hands.

OUT! WICKET! Murphy has his man! Pulls the length back a bit and bowls it wide outside off. Stokes look to clear the fence once again but does not get it from the middle. The ball goes toward the long-on region where Smith settles under it and takes a fine catch. A valiant knock of 80 from the English skipper comes to an end. England are bowled out for 237 and are trailing by just 26 runs.

... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

A good session of Test cricket! Australia got off to a great start as Pat Cummins got rid of Joe Root on the second ball of Day 2 which set the tone for them. Mitchell Starc then followed it up by removing Jonny Bairstow not long after as the visitors got a hold of the game. However, Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali stabilized things for a bit by adding 44 runs at a good rate, but a poor shot from the latter made him the next victim of Cummins. After that Chris Woakes came in and the Aussies straightaway peppered him with the short ball. He survived for a bit but gave in just before Lunch which leaves the hosts in a difficult situation. The Aussies will look to wrap up things quickly after Lunch while Stokes will look to change gears and score as many as possible. Join us at 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT) to see how things pan out in the second session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 74 runs and 4 wickets in 23.1 overs. Australia will be the happier side going into Lunch as they managed to expose the lower middle order of the hosts. However, Ben Stokes is still out there fighting for England with a glute issue and will hope to reduce the lead significantly after the break as they still trail by 121 runs with only three wickets in hand.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start Day 2! Jonny Bairstow and Joe Root are in the middle to resume their innings while Australian skipper Pat Cummins will start the proceedings on Day 3. Here we go..

Mark Wood was the wrecker in chief as he picked a five wicket haul in his comeback game. He rattled the Aussies with his sheer pace and was breathing fire at one stage. Chris Woakes and Stuart Broad shared the other 5 scalps among them ending a good effort with the ball for the Englishmen. Australia, on the other hand got into work quickly with the ball as Pat Cummins reduced the hosts to 22 for 2 sending Ben Duckett and Harry Brook early. Zak Crawley looked fluent in his 39 ball 33 but departed soon after. The local lads Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow survived a tricky few overs and ended the day at 68 for 3 trailing by 195 runs. Stay tuned as we shall be with you shortly bringing all the action on Day 2.

Australia, having put into bat first, made 263 in their 1st innings on the back of a fine counter-attacking ton by Mitchell Marsh and a handy contribution from Travis Head. The duo added 155 for the 5th wicket and got Aussies out of trouble. However, they failed to capitalize as the lower order was dismissed cheaply and the last four wickets were gone for just 18 runs.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of Day 2 in this 3rd Ashes Test. We witnessed a riveting contest on Day 1 and expect the second day to be no different. Australia will hope to pick regular wickets while England would want to take a healthy lead. We are in for an enthralling day.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from an exciting Day 1 of this 3rd Ashes Test. Both teams threw everything at each other and this is nicely poised at the moment. Day 2 may see one of them get ahead in this Test and we can expect some good cricket as well. It will start at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT), but you can join us early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Australia, on the other hand will be a bit disappointed with their batting effort. After a not-so-good start in the first session, they came back well post Lunch. Mitchell Marsh registered a brilliant hundred with good support from Travis Head as they added over 150 runs together but the former got out just before Tea. They suffered a disastrous collapse at the start of the third session as they had no answers to the pace of Mark Wood. They ended up with 263 runs on the board. They knew that they needed early breakthroughs to put pressure on the hosts and their skipper Pat Cummins led from the front with two quick wickets and then Mitchell Marsh provided them with another as they still lead by 195 runs.

England got off to the perfect start with Stuart Broad getting rid of David Warner in the very first over. The first session belonged to the English pacers, especially Wood who regularly touched speeds of over 150 clicks. They picked up four crucial wickets and it looked like they would bowl the visitors out in the second session but that was not the case as Joe Root dropped Mitchell Marsh on 12. It cost them a lot as Marsh absolutely hammered his way to a hundred and made the hosts pay before getting out to Chris Woakes just before Tea. In the third session though, the English pacers found their rhythm back and Robinson's absence did not affect them that much as they picked up the last five wickets for just 23 runs with Wood cleaning up the tail in no time. After coming out to bat, they lost Ben Duckett and Harry Brook early on but Joe Root and Zak Crawley steadied things for a bit. Unfortunately, the latter was dismissed late in the Day and Jonny Bairstow joined Root to see the rest of the session out.

A fascinating Day of Test cricket comes to an end! Session Summary - 91 runs and 8 wickets in 27.3 overs.  It was filled with wickets and runs, but mostly wickets from both sides. Mark Wood was the star of Day 1 with his brilliant five-for but a special comeback Test hundred from Mitchell Marsh brought the Aussies out of a troubling situation earlier in the Day.

Jonny Bairstow survives and Mitchell Starc ends the day with back-to-back maidens. On a good length around the top of off and angling away a touch. Bairstow hangs back and keeps it down behind point. That will also be STUMPS ON DAY 1!
